name: The Outer Wardens
flavour: They were guards in life and they are guards in death. They are bound to the vault, and they do not seem to know they are dead.

name: The Choir of Bones
flavour: Dozens of dead throats hold one note far longer than any living lungs could. The sound holds the vault's old wards together, and it has to be broken to get any deeper.

name: The Vault-Keeper
flavour: A construct built to count everyone who enters the vault and stop anyone who should not. It has been counting wrong for centuries, and it treats every living thing as a thief.

name: The Outer Palisade
flavour: Sharpened stakes, a single rope bridge, and Blackford's own soldiers, who know exactly which gaps in the wall to defend. They were trained well, by the man they are now defending.

name: The Uncrowned's Right Hand
flavour: Captain Dorran, Blackford's master-at-arms, gives the orders the soldiers actually follow. Calm, precise, and loyal to Blackford even now. He will not surrender the inner keep.

name: The Tyrant of Blackford
flavour: Lord Blackford was a good lord once. Grief made him a tyrant, and he no longer believes anyone has the right to judge him, not the Crown and not the guild.

name: The Field of Failed Guilds
flavour: The shore at the end of the road is covered in the wreckage of guilds that tried this before: banners in the sand, broken boats, and no sign anyone walked away. Every one of them came a different way. Every one of them ended up here.

name: The Silence Where Prayer Used to Work
flavour: An ancient altar stands in a ring of kneeling dead: pilgrims who came here to die, as the old rites said to. The god's last power still answers the altar, but it no longer knows the difference between finishing the rite and refusing to let anyone leave.

name: What Is Left of It
flavour: What remains of the Last God is enormous and very weak, starved for centuries. It reaches for the guild the way it reached for every pilgrim, not out of hate but because it no longer knows who it is reaching for. The guild has to hold on until it finally stops fighting, and then walk it the rest of the way.

name: The Hatchling Brood
flavour: They are young, and young dragons make mistakes: flying too close, breathing fire too early, giving away their position. That is the only reason this fight is survivable. There are a lot of them.

name: The Wyrm Keepers
flavour: Not cultists, just locals who found a brood too dangerous to kill and decided feeding it was safer. They have kept it hidden for years, they know where every hatchling is, and they will not stop now.

name: The Frozen Wyrm
flavour: The matriarch who laid the first clutch, centuries old and as big as a barn. The cold does not slow her down. She has lived up here long enough to stop noticing it.

name: What Still Guards It
flavour: The halls are guarded by demons who answer to nobody now, held in line by promises of what is waiting on the other side of the breach.

name: The Council
flavour: The lieutenants do not agree on much, including what exactly is supposed to come through the breach. They agree that this is their best chance to open it, and none of them will wait for a better one.

name: The Breach
flavour: On the far side of the half-open breach is something that has not fully arrived. It is close enough to reach through, and reaching through is all it needs to do to be a problem.

name: The Keepers
flavour: They tend the nest: clearing debris, warming the eggs, and warning off anyone who comes close with fire meant to scare first and kill second.

name: The Hatchlings
flavour: A whole clutch, already hatched and already breathing fire they cannot aim yet. Wading through a dozen of them is worse than fighting one that can.

name: The Brood Mother
flavour: She is old, enormous, and far less patient than her keepers. She knows how many of her hatchlings the guild has already killed.

name: The Marrow Eater
flavour: Ostrel's guardian: dozens of bodies stitched together into one creature with far too many arms. Built by someone with a lot of practice and no sense of style.

name: The Phylactery
flavour: A small box hidden behind an ossuary wall, beating faintly like a heart. It is what keeps Ostrel alive. Finding it is the hard part. Smashing it is easy.

name: The Lich
flavour: With his phylactery gone, Ostrel can die like anyone else, but he still fights like a lich who has had ninety years to practise. He is furious about the interruption.

name: The Presiding Intelligence
flavour: The Loom has no mouth of its own, so it speaks through every threaded person nearby at once, arguing with the guild in a dozen borrowed voices. When arguing stops working, it reaches for the guild with its threads, the same way it reached for Millbrook.
